Same group (IPNA-CSIC / Univ. La Laguna; shared authors Jimenez-Arias, Morales-Sierra, Borges, Luis) and same 7-day 150-cell-tray tomato seedling WD protocol (50% vs 100% field capacity, half-strength Hoagland, 20 seedlings/treatment, triplicate, oven-dry 70C 3 d, RGR formula): study 1 p.3 sec 2.4 cites 189 as the method (SRC-1fee2cd6baa40dd028204398). But experiments, arms and data are distinct. (1) Arms: study 1 tests nine Tenerife seaweed extracts (B. hamifera...H. scoparia, collected 2021-2022, Table 1 p.3) plus Kelpak and Sealgae at 1% w/v, 5 mL root (p.3); 189 tests 12 pure molecules (Put, Spd, N-Spd, Spm, N-Spm, Mel, Pr, Pyg, BABA, GB, Na-Si, K-Si) plus Kelpak at (5)% (Table 1 p.5, SRC-182042df70676f1c44c788cd). Only Kelpak product name overlaps, at a different dose (1% vs 5%), and no seaweed arm of study 1 appears in 189. (2) Conditions: study 1 cv. Robin, 24+/-2C, RH 65+/-2% (p.3); 189 cultivar unstated, 20-27C, RH 60-75% (p.3, SRC-1e21ab9d04a3fe289c94efd7). (3) Numeric vectors differ, so controls are not shared: study 1 Fig 2 (p.8, SRC-bb35eedae6626610a318bcf7) WW line ~300 mg, WD line ~267 mg (text p.7: WD reduced 11.2%), Kelpak bar ~268 mg; Fig 3A WW ~312, WD ~210 mg; Table 3 p.7 RGR WW 0.16, WD 0.14, Kelpak 0.15 (SRC-58f05468d2025fbc2fdb22db). Study 189 Fig 7A (p.10, SRC-a7cbb7db0a5541098034ecdb) WW ~330 mg, WD ~207 mg, Kelp ~228 mg; RGR in % with WW ~17.6, WD ~11; Table 3 printed DW WW 260+/-25, WD 193+/-32 mg; text reports ~25% WD reduction. (4) Timing: 189 received 14 Feb 2022/published 17 Mar 2022; study 1 is a 2023 article with different aims (seaweed bioprospecting, NMR, ABA-reporter). No duplicate, preprint, companion or shared-control relation; retain both studies fully and independently.

398 (Duc & Posta 2018, Columella, DOI 10.18380/SZIE.COLUM.2018.5.2.7; receipts SRC-f635eb4d408df68813725267 p3, SRC-39fe645f5cf3f316975a6d79 p4, SRC-caa094c41060a9031eef70af p5) and the PPB accepted manuscript (Duc, Csintalan & Posta, DOI 10.1016/j.plaphy.2018.09.011; receipts SRC-edb85f10211fa842ea3657c1 p1, SRC-43a9fb257663b660f99b81a5 p5, SRC-d3f69b0e030ef6ebdcc61dc4 p6, SRC-2237e34af9c195cc62c70bbe p9, SRC-c217a1b10c966b8f80202a11 p10, SRC-43eaefcde6a94fe68244d5c8 p26, SRC-f3a0c46e3ff7bb3cf8cac509 p27) describe the same experiment. Shared design: tomato MoneyMaker; 0.5 L pots of 0.5 kg 4:1 sand:loamy soil with identical soil chemistry (pH 7.1, 1.61% OM, N 15.6, P 36, K 60 mg/kg); S. constrictum inoculum 30 g/pot at 27 spores/g versus autoclaved inoculum plus 3 ml <20 um filtrate; EKOCHIL 1500 chamber at 26/20 C, 16/8 h, 600 umol m-2 s-1, 60% RH; Long Ashton solution with 3.2 uM P; stress applied at 6 weeks as 42 C for 6 h versus non-stress; analyses n=4 per group, mean+-SD. Numeric overlap, 398 Fig 1 and Fig 2 versus PPB Fig 3, Fig 4 and Table 2, for non-AM and S. constrictum under non-stress and heat. Colonization: 398 text 73% non-stress and 68% heat; PPB Table 2 gives 73.60 +- 8.14 and 67.87 +- 5.55. MDA (nmol/g FW), read graphically: 398 Fig 1B and PPB Fig 3A both show about 1.32 and 1.28 non-stress (non-AM, AM) and about 1.87 and 1.54 under heat; 398 text says non-AM +42% and AM 17% lower, and PPB text says 17-18% lower. H2O2: both figures show about 1.0 and 0.97 non-stress and about 6.0 and 3.6 under heat; both texts say six-fold increase in non-AM and 40% reduction in AM under heat. Enzymes: 398 Fig 2A-F and PPB Fig 4A-F show matching bars and error bars, for example root SOD under heat about 18 for non-AM and about 34 for AM; root CAT under heat about 0.30 and 0.40 with a large AM error bar; leaf POD about 1.93, 2.3, 3.4 and 3.75. Every data item in 398 is therefore contained in the PPB study; 398 has no unique data (no tables, no yield or biomass). PPB is canonical because it also holds the S. deserticola and drought arms, dry weights, gs, RWC, Fv/Fm and gene expression, which 398 lacks. The reported plant counts differ (24 vs 120 plants) but the n=4 groups and values coincide. 398 must not be counted as independent evidence.

Different publications and experiments from the same lab (same four authors Rojas-Solis, Vences-Guzman, Sohlenkamp, Santoyo; Santoyo lab, UMSNH Morelia). 705 (SRC-fd8fd3b2be6363bcfe872149 p1) is the bioRxiv preprint doi 10.1101/2022.10.19.512789, posted 19 Oct 2022, on Pseudomonas fluorescens UM270 and its cardiolipin-synthase deletion mutants clsA/clsB. D_7885f42a29464ee5 (SRC-3928a902041dee78e0db801d p1) is the Current Microbiology paper doi 10.1007/s00284-020-02069-1, published 5 Jun 2020, on Bacillus toyonensis COPE52. The two are different DOIs, species and treatments, so this is not a PREPRINT_OF pair (the 2022 preprint is not an earlier version of the 2020 article). Both use tomato cv Saladette, one plant per pot, 0/100/200 mM NaCl irrigation every third day and 5-week evaluation, which follows the lab's shared protocol (cites Rojas-Solis 2018). Treatments and sample sizes differ. 705 has an uninoculated control plus UM270 WT, deltaclsA and deltaclsB, 12 plants per treatment (Methods 2.8, Table 6 footnote), 12 arms. D_7885 (SRC-d440f28029764d4010aba20c p4) has control vs COPE52 only, 24 plants per treatment, 6 arms, and inoculum 1x10^8 CFU/mL. Numeric vectors differ, so there are no shared controls. 705 control plant dry weight (g) is 0.116, 0.067, 0.049 at 0, 100, 200 mM (SRC-25508359012fe071e4d6b6c8 p30 Table 6). D_7885 Fig. 2e (SRC-e271af7b70dc79ff392600ea p7) shows control dry weight of about 0.68, 0.18 and 0.09 g. Control root length is 14.22/10.6/6.4 cm in 705 and about 20.5/13.5/8.5 cm in D_7885, and control shoot length is 10.33/9.93/6.77 cm in 705 and about 20/12.5/10.5 cm in D_7885. D_7885 reports its tomato results only in Fig. 2 (bars, mean +/- SE), with no printed table of means. The values of the two studies are different and independent, so neither contains the other's data.
